Getting your first LSA leads but not sure why some cost $5 and others cost $50?

Most window cleaners starting out set their bid once and never touch it again. The algorithm doesn't work that way — it needs regular adjustments based on job types, your close rate, and what competitors are doing in your zip code.

Managed LSAs for a window/power washing company last year. $4,202 in ad spend → $18,907 in revenue. $22 cost per lead, 50 jobs closed.

The difference between average results and those numbers? Daily bid management and disputing every bad lead for a full refund.

Happy to break down how it works if you're curious. Drop a comment or shoot me a DM.

What's your current cost per lead on LSA?

If you don't know off the top of your head, that's the first problem. The second is probably that you're paying for leads you shouldn't be.

Google will charge you for hang-up calls, wrong numbers, and people who dialed you by accident. You can dispute those and get your money back — but most operators don't because the process isn't obvious.

We manage LSA campaigns daily for home service businesses. Dispute bad leads, pace budgets, optimize bids by job type.

One window/power washing client: $22 CPL, 4.5x ROAS for the full year. If you're not seeing numbers like that, it might be worth a conversation.

DM me or drop a comment.

Anyone else notice LSA performance drops off hard in certain months unless you're actively managing it?

Google's algorithm is sensitive. Budget pacing, bid settings, review velocity — if any of those slip, your placement tanks and your CPL doubles.

Managed LSAs for a power/window washing company all through 2025. Full year: $4,202 spent, $18,907 generated, 148 leads, 50 jobs closed. 4.5x return, $22 per lead.

None of that happens on autopilot. It's daily check-ins, disputes on bad leads, and ongoing bid adjustments.

If your LSA feels inconsistent or you're not sure if you're getting the most from your spend, drop a comment or DM me.

How much of your LSA budget went to leads that never booked?

Google counts a lot of calls as "leads" that aren't. Voicemails. People asking about a service you don't offer. Spam. You can fight those back and get refunded — but it takes knowing the process and doing it consistently.

We manage LSA campaigns for pressure washers and other home service trades. Daily budget monitoring, bid optimization by job type, and lead dispute management.

The businesses we work with are paying for actual customers, not junk calls.

If you're running LSAs and want to know if you're leaving money on the table, DM me or comment below.

Honest question — are you actually checking your LSA campaign every day?

Most people set it and forget it. And Google quietly raises your cost per lead, drifts your service area, or starts sending you leads you can't close.

The fix isn't complicated, it's just consistent work. Daily bid checks, disputing bad leads, keeping your Google Business Profile dialed in.

I manage this daily for pressure washing businesses. One client in the exterior cleaning space did 4.5x ROAS on their LSA spend last year.

Happy to walk anyone through what a dialed-in campaign actually looks like. Drop a question below or send me a DM.

Quick poll — how many of you have ever disputed a lead on LSA?

Most haven't. And that's fine, the process isn't obvious. But Google will charge you for calls that don't qualify — calls under 30 seconds, people asking for something you don't do, wrong numbers. Those are disputable. Every refund you get back compounds over the year.

I run LSA management for home service businesses, pressure washing included. Between disputes, daily bid optimization, and job type targeting, it moves the needle.

4.5x ROAS for a power washing client over 12 months. Real number, real campaign.

Anyone curious how the dispute process works, happy to explain in the comments.

$4.10 per lead from Google LSA. 1,003 leads in a year. Anyone else hitting numbers like that?

Full year 2025 from a car detailing client: $4,713 in ad spend → $86,995 in revenue. 18.4x ROAS. 341 jobs closed.

That's not luck. It's daily bid management, disputing every junk lead for a full refund, and keeping the Google Business Profile dialed in. Car detailing is actually one of the better-performing trades on LSA when the campaign is set up and managed correctly.

Most detail shops I've talked to either aren't on LSA yet or set it up once and got inconsistent results. The setup and the ongoing management are two completely different things.

If you're curious how to get to $4 CPL, drop a comment or DM me.

Plumbers are some of the highest-paying leads on Google LSA — which also means a poorly managed campaign bleeds money fast.

The higher your average ticket, the more a bad lead actually costs you. And Google will serve you leads outside your service area, for jobs you don't do, or calls that were clearly misdials. Those are disputable and refundable — but most plumbing shops don't have time to chase them.

We manage LSA campaigns daily for home service businesses. Bad leads get disputed. Bids get adjusted by job type. Budget pacing prevents you from blowing through your monthly spend by week two.

If you're running LSAs and not hitting consistent results, drop a comment or shoot me a DM. Happy to look at what you've got.

scripts.group: Landscape and Lawn Care in Florida
scripts.content:
Florida landscapers — LSA has a solid spring window right now and most of you are probably leaving leads on the table.

The algorithm rewards consistent engagement. If your bids have been sitting untouched since last fall, your cost per lead going into the busy season is higher than it needs to be.

We manage LSA campaigns for home service businesses, and lawn/landscaping in Florida is one of the better-performing categories because of the year-round demand and consistent search volume.

Daily bid optimization, lead dispute management, and Google Business Profile maintenance are the core of what we do.

If you want to go into spring with a campaign that's actually dialed, drop a comment or DM me.

What are you paying per lead on LSA for junk removal? Because $22 or under is doable — and most operators are paying double that.

Junk removal is competitive on LSA, but the operators who do well actively manage their campaigns. Bid by job type, dispute bad leads, keep your response rate up. It's daily work, but it compounds.

I manage LSA for home service businesses. We track cost per lead, revenue generated, and dispute any lead that doesn't qualify. Every refund adds up.

If you're running LSA and not actively monitoring it, you're almost certainly overpaying. DM me or drop a comment if you want to compare numbers.

If you've got LSA running and you haven't disputed a single lead this month, you're leaving money behind.

Google charges you for calls that don't qualify. Spam, wrong numbers, calls for services you don't offer — those are all disputable. But it takes knowing what to flag and following up consistently.

On top of that, bid strategy for junk removal varies by job type. A full cleanout shouldn't have the same bid setting as a single-item pickup.

We manage LSA daily for home service operators — disputes, bid optimization, budget pacing. Not a set-it-and-forget-it situation.

Happy to do a quick audit of your current setup. Drop a comment or DM me.

Most GCs and subs on LSA are funding Google's margins more than their own pipeline.

The default settings are not optimized for your business. Google wants you to spend fast and wide. Your job is to spend narrow and efficient — right service area, right job types, right bids.

We manage LSA for home service and contractor businesses. Daily bid management, lead dispute management (bad leads get credited back), and budget pacing so you're not out of budget by Thursday every week.

If you're running Google LSA and want to know what a professionally managed campaign looks like, drop a comment or send me a DM.

Painting is one of those trades where LSA can be incredible or a total waste — and the difference is almost entirely in how the campaign is managed.

Interior vs. exterior, residential vs. commercial — Google doesn't automatically optimize for what's most profitable for you. That's manual work. So is disputing leads that don't qualify (wrong service area, calls under 30 seconds, people asking about something you don't do).

We manage LSA campaigns for painters and other home service trades. Daily bid optimization, dispute management, budget pacing.

If you're running LSA and feel like you're not getting the return you should be, drop a comment or DM me.

Genuine question for this group — when cleaning business owners ask you about paid lead generation, what do you tell them about Google LSA?

A lot of cleaning businesses I've talked to are either not on LSA at all or they set one up and it's just sitting there unmanaged.

LSA for residential cleaning can perform really well. Good ticket size, high repeat client value, strong search intent. But the campaign has to be actively managed — bids adjusted, bad leads disputed, GBP kept current.

I run LSA management for home service businesses. Happy to be a resource here if anyone has questions about how it works for cleaning businesses specifically. Drop them in the comments.

Handyman LSA is underrated. And most guys running it are paying too much per lead because nobody's actively managing the campaign.

You can dispute leads that don't qualify. You can bid differently for small jobs vs. larger ones. You can pace your budget so you're not out of spend before the weekend. These aren't tricks — they're just daily maintenance that most operators skip.

We manage Google LSA for home service businesses including handyman operators. The focus is keeping cost per lead low and making sure every dollar is working.

If you're running LSA or thinking about starting, drop a comment or DM me.

Roofing is one of the highest CPL trades on LSA — which makes it one of the highest stakes to manage badly.

If you're paying $100+ per lead and a chunk of those are junk (spam, wrong area, calls that had nothing to do with roofing), that's real money. Those leads are disputable and refundable. But it takes process and consistency to actually get the money back.

We manage Google LSA for home service businesses. Daily bid management, lead dispute management, budget pacing. High-ticket trades like roofing are exactly where active campaign management pays for itself.

Drop a comment or DM me if you want to compare what a managed campaign produces vs. what you're seeing now.
